The knowledge distillation paradigm distills knowledge from the teacher model to a student model, which is beneficial to improve the results [11]. To mitigate the adverse impact of depth error in the pseudo ground-truth, we apply a multi-view check filter [25] to filter out erroneous depth. The knowledge distillation loss is thus defined as LKD = X p Φ(p) ⊙ � Dt (p) − Dpseudo (p)  , (10) where Φ(p) stands for the multi-view check filter, ⊙ denotes the element-wise multiplication. The core principle of multi- view check is similar to that of the novel view synthesis. We draw on Eq. 5 to get each projected point pt→s in the source view and acquire a warped depth map, Ds→t(p) = Ds pt→s , (11) where Ds stands for the depth map of source frame. Similar to the projection procedure above, we leverage Ds to perform a reprojection procedure to acquire each reprojected 2D point eps→t and depth map eD s→t (p) in the target view.
